comparison.query: Compare the importance of 'mean smoothness' versus 'worst smoothness' in the context of malignancy prediction based on known medical literature and feature distributions.

result.explanation: In medical literature, smoothness is a well-established texture feature in breast cancer classification. The 'worst' smoothness feature reflects the most extreme value across all tumor regions, which is more indicative of malignancy due to the irregular cell morphology seen in malignant tumors. According to the Breast Cancer Wisconsin (Diagnostic) Data Set, 'worst smoothness' has been shown to have stronger predictive power than 'mean smoothness' because it captures the most pathological characteristics of tumor heterogeneity. Additionally, in this dataset, 'worst smoothness' has a higher correlation with malignancy outcomes than its mean counterpart. Therefore, masking the worst smoothness feature is likely to significantly alter the model's prediction, whereas masking mean smoothness would have a smaller impact.
